causalModel.founding: Riverwalk is a halt in a sheltered sea cove at the mouth of the pilgrim water, which is the channel up to Hissmir. Boats off the Padomaic run put in at Riverwalk. The houses stand along the plank walk, which serves as the village street.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The cove is the only sheltered water on this coast stretch. Thorn lies under a kilometre from Riverwalk by the Tear road, which leaves the village westward. Canoes leave the ferry stage for Hissmir and Murkwater.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The villagers earn their living from the ferry stage and the toll. The toll falls on boats entering the pilgrim water. The villagers feed and lodge the boat crews.
causalModel.pressures: Thorn's field-owners say the toll on the pilgrim water is theirs. The stewards of Hissmir make the same claim to the toll on the pilgrim water.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the cove silted up, boats would bypass Riverwalk. The villagers sound the way across the cove every morning. The way leads to the ferry stage.

districts.notes: Plank walks over a cove joining a dry spit to a dry islet, with a ferry landing off the islet.

why.what: District 0 holds the cove, the boards over it, the spit and the islet. The spit lies at the head of the boards. The islet lies at the foot of the boards.
why.whyHere: The shallows between the spit and the islet carry the tracks from the west.
why.whySpot: The cove lies under a cliff. The cliff shelters the cove from the open sea.
why.whyNeighbours: Hissmir and Murkwater lie west of Riverwalk. The boat lane runs past the islet.
why.playerPurpose: Riverwalk offers rest, trade, the toll and the ferry.
why.microGeography: The cove holds knee-deep black water over mud. Two low mud shelves lie either side of the water.

districts.notes: The long house on its stilts in the cove, with its plank landing to the spit.

why.what: The long house stands on stilts in the cove water. The long house has a landing.
why.whyHere: The boat crews tie up in the cove. The household built the long house out over the cove.
why.whySpot: The long house stands in the deepest water by the spit. A boat can lie alongside the stilts there.
why.whyNeighbours: The spit and the head of the boards lie a few steps west. They lie across the landing from the long house.
why.playerPurpose: The household feeds the boat crews.
why.microGeography: The water is knee-deep black water over mud. It lies off the dry edge of the spit.

districts.notes: The crews' house and a family house on the dry spit at the head of the boards. Both are plank houses in the style of the coast's trade ports. No other houses in the village are built this way.

why.what: Two plank houses stand on the dry spit. The spit lies at the head of the boards.
why.whyHere: The spit is the only dry ground at the north end of the cove. The households built their houses on the spit.
why.whySpot: The houses stand on the level top of the spit. The spit lies between the shrine and the long house landing.
why.whyNeighbours: The shrine and the start of the boards lie a few steps south. The long house stands in the water to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The houses offer a safe room for the night. The household's stores are kept in the houses behind shut doors.
why.microGeography: The spit has dry sandy ground. The ground is levelled into two pads.

parcels.orientationWhy: The boards run straight from flat ground at the spit's south shore to the islet. This is the shortest line over the water. Every walker passes the toll.

playerPurpose.note: The toll holder takes the toll from every walker on the boards. The nightly argument over it ends in an accusation that can be proved.
The nightly toll argument plays out on the boards between the spit and the islet.
Old planks lie beside new ones here. The difference between them is proof in the toll accusation.

why.what: The long walk is a plank span on piles. It runs from the spit straight across the cove to the islet.
why.whyHere: The channel is the street. The boards carry the tracks over knee-deep water. Water covers the channel at every step.
why.whySpot: The long walk starts on flat ground at the spit's south shore. It runs straight across the cove to the islet's north shore.
why.whyNeighbours: The long house stands in the water off the spit. It stands near the head of the boards.
why.playerPurpose: The long walk is the way through the village. It crosses the cove to the islet and the ferry. The west boards join it halfway.
why.microGeography: The planks sit a hand's breadth over black water. They stand on sunk piles. The boards are of different ages.

parcels.orientationWhy: Three spans run from the islet's north-east shore. They run out to the point where the bed drops away.

why.what: The ferry landing has three plank spans. The spans run from the islet out to deep water.
why.whyHere: The raft draws more water than the cove holds.
why.whySpot: The landing starts on the islet's north-east shore. That shore is the nearest dry footing to water that is deep enough for the raft.
why.whyNeighbours: The stage shelter stands behind the landing. The raft lies at the end of the landing.
why.playerPurpose: The landing is the way from the islet to the ferry raft.
why.microGeography: The planks sit a hand's breadth over the water. They run out to the point where the bed drops away.

parcels.orientationWhy: The crews' house door faces south. The door opens onto the path from the head of the boards.

playerPurpose.note: The household sells rope, food and boat stores.
A room with a door that shuts: the safest bed in the village.

why.what: The crews' house is a plank house on the spit. The household lets beds to boat crews there. The household also sells stores to boat crews there.
why.whyHere: The villagers earn their living from crews that stop halfway along the coast lane. The crews pay for a bed with a door that shuts.
why.whySpot: The crews' house stands on the dry top of the spit. It stands a step from the head of the boards. The toll-holder's post stands nearby.
why.whyNeighbours: The family house and the shrine stand a few steps east. The long house stands in the water beyond them.
why.playerPurpose: The crews' house offers a safe bed behind a shut door. It also holds stores for the water.
why.microGeography: The crews' house is a plank house on a levelled pad on the spit. Its door opens over the path.

why.whyHere: The households that keep the boards live beside them. They live on the only dry ground in the cove.
why.whySpot: The family house stands at the east end of the spit. It stands beside the shrine and clear of the path.
why.whyNeighbours: The crews' house and its yard lie a few steps west. The long house landing lies just east.

parcels.orientationWhy: The long house has an open front and a landing. Both face west to the spit. They also face the path from the head of the boards.

playerPurpose.note: An open plank house where the household sleeps on the floor and feeds the boat crews.

why.what: The long house is an open plank house on piles in the cove. The household sleeps there. The boat crews eat there and sleep in the crews' house.
why.whyHere: The villagers earn their living from crews that stop halfway along the coast lane. The crews sleep in the crews' house. They eat in the long house.
why.whySpot: The long house stands in the shallows off the spit's east shore. A short landing reaches it from the path at the head of the boards.
why.whyNeighbours: The crews' house stands on the spit beside the landing path. The boards start below the shrine.
why.playerPurpose: The long house shelters the household and is where the crews eat. It is entered from its landing.
why.microGeography: The long house is a plank house on piles in knee-deep water. Its landing is laid against the open front.

parcels.orientationWhy: The stage shelter's open front turns west. It faces the path from the foot of the long walk.

why.what: The stage shelter is an open tent. The stage-mistress takes the fares there.
why.whyHere: The ferry is the village's living. The ferry lands on the islet.
why.whySpot: The stage shelter stands on the islet's east shelf. It stands beside the ferry landing.
why.whyNeighbours: The ferry landing runs out from the shore north of the shelter.
why.microGeography: The stage shelter is a hide tent. It stands on a low mud pad on the islet.

parcels.orientationWhy: The raft lies off the end of the landing. Passengers board it there.

playerPurpose.note: The stage mistress works the ferry raft. Thorn and Hissmir both tax the cove. Paying either counts as taking its side.

why.what: The ferry raft is moored off the end of the landing.
why.whyHere: Passengers and freight cross on the raft. They cross to the other stations of the lane.
why.whySpot: The raft lies in the first water that is deep enough to float it. That water is north of the islet.
why.whyNeighbours: The landing runs out to the raft from the islet.
why.playerPurpose: The ferry raft carries passengers along the coast lane.
why.microGeography: The water is more than a metre deep. It lies over a level bed.

parcels.orientationWhy: The totems face the long house yard.

why.what: A small shrine of totems and a chime stands on the spit.
why.whyHere: Crews leave an offering at the shrine. They leave it before they go back on the water.
why.whySpot: The shrine stands on the spit's flat ground. It stands by the path to the long house landing.
why.whyNeighbours: The head of the boards lies a few steps from the shrine.
why.playerPurpose: A blessing can be received at the shrine before the water.
why.microGeography: The shrine stands on the spit's dry mud. It stands by the path to the long house.

parcels.orientationWhy: The side boards run due west from the crossing on the long walk. They run to the point where the track from the west leaves the shallows.

why.what: The west boards are two plank spans from the crossing on the long walk. They end in a flight of steps down into the water.
why.whyHere: Walkers on the track from the western villages wade the shallows. They climb out of the water onto the boards here.
why.whySpot: The west boards lie halfway along the long walk. They lie level with the point where the track reaches the cove.
why.whyNeighbours: The long walk crosses at the east end of the west boards. The toll and the long house lie north. The islet and the ferry lie south.
why.playerPurpose: The west boards are the way in from the west. Steps lead up from the shallows onto the boards.
why.microGeography: The water is knee-deep black water over soft mud. The lowest steps stand under the surface.

routes.why: Route 0 is the last stretch of the track from the west. It reaches the boards halfway across the cove.
Route 1 runs from the boards laid before the crews' house door to the head of the long walk; it stops at the boards, never at the sill.
Route 2 runs from the long house yard to the shrine.
Route 3 crosses the islet from the boards to the ferry landing.
Route 4 runs from the islet path to the stage shelter.
Route 5 runs from the head of the boards across the spit to the long house landing.
Route 6 is the short spur from the boards off the family house's porch to the hut path; it stops at the boards, never at the sill.
The silted flat along the line the sounded way ran east from the raft, mud where the boats once passed.

occupants.cultureRole: A boardwalk household keeps the long house.
A boat crew stops for the night.

approaches.sequence: Travellers come along the track from the west. The line of boards shows first across the water. The long house then shows in the water off the spit near the head of the boards. The stage shelter shows on the islet at the foot of the boards.
approaches.wayfinding: The track meets the boards at their midpoint. The toll and the long house lie north. The islet and the ferry lie south and then east.

networkTerminals.why: The tracks from the villages to the west come across the shallows. They end on the boards halfway across the cove.

combatSpaces.why: The dry spit lies at the head of the boards. It is the open footing in the village.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The settlement-register row Riverwalk is a boardwalk village on the coast lane. The record lists occupants of D1 households, D2 crews and D2 toll hands. The notable slots are toll-holder and stage-mistress.
scaleGrounding.why: The crews' house and a family house stand on the spit. The long house stands on piles in the shallows beside them. The islet takes the stage tent. Three plank walks join the buildings. A shrine and a ferry raft complete the village.

candidates.why: A dry spit and a dry islet lie either side of a knee-deep cove. The site lies on the line that the western tracks already follow. Water deep enough for a ferry lies off the islet.
The plotted anchor lies in the middle of the cove.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The water there is under 1 m deep and offers no dry footing. Buildings stand on dry ground in this village.
